title: Master My Stories: Staying in Dialogue When You're Upset
coreMove: Work backward from your reaction to the story you told, then separate facts from interpretation before acting.
sourcePressure: The Path to Action inserts a story between facts and feelings, exposing victim, villain, and helpless stories as editable interpretations rather than direct reality.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Teaching readers to distrust emotion or suppress anger.
sourceAnchorsNote: source contains no named anecdote for this chapter

hook: dictionary definition of a crucial conversation
tryThisNow: pick a conversation and journal about it without a chapter-specific test
examples: manager feedback in a conference room
spouse argument at the kitchen counter
student raising hand in a classroom

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: prevents the timestamp+named-protagonist template from dominating the chapter

exampleSpecs.domain: pharmacy counter where a technician assumes a customer is abusing the refill system
exampleSpecs.audience: a pharmacy technician who is tired of being yelled at during shortage season
exampleSpecs.stakes: a diabetic patient may leave without insulin because the technician acts from a villain story
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the technician feels the snap rising, pauses with the refill screen open, and lists the actual facts before deciding what story is fair
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A gray refill screen flashes rejected in red behind the pharmacy counter.

exampleSpecs.domain: airport gate crew after a delayed boarding announcement
exampleSpecs.audience: a gate agent interpreting a pilot's silence as arrogance
exampleSpecs.stakes: a full flight may turn hostile if the crew fights each other in front of passengers
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: after a curt announcement, the agent reconstructs see-hear-story-feel-act and finds the missing maintenance fact under her anger
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "Wait," someone says, and a boarding scanner sits idle while Zone 2 passengers crowd the stanchions.

exampleSpecs.domain: animal shelter adoption desk when a volunteer thinks an applicant is careless
exampleSpecs.audience: a shelter volunteer protective of a returned dog
exampleSpecs.stakes: a good adoption could be blocked by a victim story about overworked staff and careless applicants
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the volunteer hears herself saying people like this, stops, and asks what facts she actually has about the applicant's fenced yard and prior vet records
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The first signal is sensory before it is social: a leash with a red adoption tag hangs from a pegboard hook.

exampleSpecs.domain: restaurant expo line where a sous-chef assumes sabotage after a repeated plating mistake
exampleSpecs.audience: a sous-chef on a slammed Saturday service
exampleSpecs.stakes: the line could melt down because one cook gets branded lazy instead of trained on the new garnish order
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the sous-chef predicts what his helpless story will make him do, then checks the printed ticket and sees the new garnish abbreviation was never explained
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You notice a heat lamp glows over three plates missing the same garnish before anyone names the problem.

exampleSpecs.domain: grant-funded research lab after a data file is mislabeled
exampleSpecs.audience: a principal investigator who feels betrayed by a graduate assistant
exampleSpecs.stakes: months of trust and a publication deadline depend on whether she checks the story before accusing
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the investigator opens the file history, separates the timestamp facts from the betrayal story, and asks one counter-question before sending the email
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Only later does the miss become obvious: a file named final_final2.csv sits in a shared drive folder.

exampleSpecs.domain: fire station equipment bay after a missing oxygen cylinder check
exampleSpecs.audience: a lieutenant convinced a probie is careless
exampleSpecs.stakes: crew trust and emergency readiness suffer if the lieutenant acts from a villain story
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the lieutenant sees anger in his own clipped gear check, backs up to the facts, and asks why a reasonable rookie might have missed the second cylinder
exampleSpecs.firstImage: What changes when a silver oxygen cylinder lies strapped into an open rescue compartment?

skillTargets: separate observable fact from added meaning
identify victim, villain, and helpless stories in live irritation
choose a revised action after the story changes

tryThisNowSpec: Pick one irritation from today. Write four labels in order: saw/heard, story, feeling, action. Under saw/heard, keep only what a camera or recorder would capture.

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm — a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following 'concrete anchor -> abstract rule -> elaboration'
